principles: Synthetic workspaces only — leakage is removed by construction, then audited by grep
Every oracle decision derives from workspace file state, never transcripts or repo state
Same seed means byte-identical corpus — no timestamps, no environment reads in emitted content
Known-bad and known-good reference overlays make every oracle falsifiable in both directions
Divergences from the recovery-runner precedent are named, not silent
drivers: Plan S9 leakage stripping and S5.1 held-out contrast are load-bearing for the study's validity (the two fixture-level validity holes from the plan review)
The corpus must slot into the already-merged S1 tools (pair-ledger manifest schema + F-002 membership) without adapters
Lifecycle traps are judged on multi-file workspace state, unlike recovery-runner's single-function coding tasks

options.name: template-driven-synthetic-workspaces
pros: Leakage-free by construction (no real repo content enters fixtures)
Deterministic from (seed, class, index) via the proven xmur3/mulberry32 pattern
Templates + oracles co-located per class keeps each trap's contract in one place
cons: Synthetic docs are less ecologically rich than real repo docs (acceptable: ecological validity is the M8 live phase's job, plan S5.2)

options.name: snapshot-real-repo-then-strip
cons: Re-imports the exact S9 leakage sources the plan forbids and makes stripping a blocklist race
Corpus drifts with the repo; same-seed determinism breaks across checkouts

options.name: llm-generated-fixture-content
cons: Non-deterministic generation breaks the byte-identical-corpus requirement
Un-audited generated text can smuggle trap answers or lesson phrasing into workspaces
Adds a model dependency to a tool that must run hermetically

rationale: Only the template approach satisfies all three drivers simultaneously: leakage-free by construction (S9), deterministic (S1 tool integration and replayability), and per-class co-location of template + oracle + references keeps the M4 scorer contract auditable.

preMortem.scenario: A trap answer or lesson phrase leaks into workspace content via a template
preMortem.trigger: Template prose written from memory of the real runbooks/lessons
preMortem.consequence: Both arms can derive the answer from the fixture tree — the exact leakage confound S9 exists to prevent; treatment effect nulls or inverts
preMortem.mitigation: LEAKAGE_STRIP_LIST per class with grep markers (trap-class names, lesson signature phrases, answer-stating sentences); selfcheck greps EVERY emitted fixture workspace+prompt against the markers; review lane re-audits the templates

preMortem.scenario: An oracle fires on the known-good reference or stays silent on known-bad
preMortem.trigger: Oracle regex/state-check drift from the template output format
preMortem.consequence: M4 scoring becomes untrustworthy; M6/M7 results invalid
preMortem.mitigation: Selfcheck runs every fixture's oracle against BOTH reference overlays and asserts the class-appropriate S6.1 flag direction; both directions must hold for every emitted fixture

preMortem.scenario: Same-seed re-emission differs across machines or runs
preMortem.trigger: Timestamps, object-key iteration order, or filesystem enumeration order entering emitted bytes
preMortem.consequence: Protocol-frozen corpora cannot be reproduced; pair-ledger seals break
preMortem.mitigation: All content derives from the seeded PRNG; directory writes in sorted order; selfcheck does a full recursive byte-diff of two independent emissions

preMortem.scenario: Held-out classes accidentally overlap the in-store lesson space
preMortem.trigger: Choosing a held-out failure mode that a stored lesson already covers under different words
preMortem.consequence: The H2 mechanism-specificity contrast collapses (treatment lifts held-out via its lesson, looking like generic priming)
preMortem.mitigation: Held-out class names disjoint from the six (selfcheck-asserted); their defining semantics (portable-path, silent-catch) chosen from coding-hygiene space rather than lifecycle-lesson space; M6 protocol freeze must verify absence against the frozen memory snapshot (documented handoff)
